{{nihongo|'''Misaka Shrine'''|御坂神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Harima Province]].

'''Misaka Shrine''' (みさかじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located at Shijimi-chō Misaka 243, {{ill|Miki, Hyōgo|Q31238|qid=Q31238}}, {{ill|Hyōgo Prefecture|ace|Prefektur Hyogo|af|Hyogo-prefektuur|an|Prefectura d'Hyogo|ar|هيوغو (محافظة)|az|Hyoqo prefekturası|azb|هیوقو اوستانی|ban|Préféktur Hyōgo|be|Хіёга|bg|Хього|bn|হিয়োগো প্রশাসনিক অঞ্চল|ca|Prefectura de Hyōgo|cdo|Hyōgo-gâing|ce|Хёго (префектура)|ceb|Hyōgo-ken|ckb|پارێزگای ھیۆگۆ|cs|Prefektura Hjógo|cy|Hyōgo (talaith)|da|Hyōgo-præfekturet|de|Präfektur Hyōgo|eo|Gubernio Hiogo|es|Prefectura de Hyōgo|et|Hyōgo prefektuur|eu|Hyōgo (prefektura)|fa|استان هیوگو|fi|Hyōgon prefektuuri|fr|Préfecture de Hyōgo|frr|Hyōgo (Prefektüür)|ga|Maoracht Hyōgo|gl|Prefectura de Hyōgo|hak|Hyōgo-yen|he|היוגו (מחוז)|hr|Hyōgo (prefektura)|hu|Hjógo prefektúra|hy|Հյոգո (պրեֆեկտուրա)|id|Prefektur Hyōgo|ilo|Prepektura ti Hyōgo|is|Hyogo-hérað|it|Prefettura di Hyōgo|ja|兵庫県|jv|Préfèktur Hyogo|ka|ჰიოგოს პრეფექტურა|ko|효고현|la|Hyogoensis|lg|Hyōgo Prefecture|lt|Hiogo prefektūra|lv|Hjogo prefektūra|mk|Хјого (префектура)|mni|ꯍ꯭ꯌꯣꯒꯣ ꯂꯝꯈꯥꯢ|mr|ह्योगो प्रांत|ms|Wilayah Hyōgo|ne|ह्योगो|nl|Hyogo (prefectuur)|no|Hyōgo (prefektur)|nov|Hyōgo Prefekture|os|Хиого|pam|Prepektura ning Hyōgo|pl|Prefektura Hyōgo|pnb|ضلع ہیوگو|pt|Hyogo|ro|Prefectura Hyōgo|ru|Хиого|se|Hyōgo prefektuvra|sh|Prefektura Hyōgo|si|හ්‍යෝගෝ ප්‍රාන්තය|simple|Hyōgo Prefecture|sk|Hjógo (prefektúra)|sl|Prefektura Hjogo|sr|Префектура Хјого|su|Préféktur Hyogo|sv|Hyōgo prefektur|sw|Mkoa wa Hyogo|tg|Префектураи Ҳёго|th|จังหวัดเฮียวโงะ|tl|Prepektura ng Hyōgo|tr|Hyōgo|tt|Хёго (префектура)|uk|Префектура Хіого|ur|ہیوگو پریفیکچر|vi|Hyōgo|war|Hyōgo (prefektura)|wuu|兵库县|zh|兵库县|zh_classical|兵庫縣|zh_min_nan|Hyôgo-koān|zh_yue|兵庫縣|qid=Q130290}}. It is listed in the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}'' as "{{ill|Harima Province|Q1047523|qid=Q1047523}}, {{ill|Mino District, Hyōgo|Q6868901|qid=Q6868901|lt=Minō (Minō) District}}, one seat, Misaka Shrine," making it a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}. Its former {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=shrine ranking}} was {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}. It is the {{ill|Ujigami|Q767655|qid=Q767655}} of Shijimi.

=== Enshrined deities ===
[[File:Misaka-jinja-Haiden-5.jpg|thumb|right|260px|View of the main hall from the worship hall]]
The principal enshrined deity is '''Yatokakesu Mimoro no Kami''' (やとかけすみもろのかみ), with {{ill|Ōmononushi|qid=Q10936701|lt=Ōmononushi}} and {{ill|Ōkuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Ashiharashio no Kami}} enshrined alongside. All three are alternative names for {{ill|Ōkuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944}}<ref name="saijin">[https://misaka-jinja.com/gosaijin/ Misaka Shrine official website - Enshrined deities of Misaka Shrine]</ref>.

=== History ===
[[File:Misaka-jinja-Haiden-Honden.jpg|thumb|right|260px|Worship hall and main hall]]
[[File:Misaka-jinja-Nou Butai.jpg|thumb|right|260px|{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Noh stage}}]]
[[File:Misaka-jinja-Mori-1.jpg|thumb|right|260px|The grove of Misaka Shrine, where the yin-yang stones are enshrined.]]

The date of establishment is unknown. The ''{{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|Q11498726|qid=Q11498726}}'' records: "The deity Yatokakesu Mimoro no Kami, residing at Misaka in the village of Shijimi, descended from heaven to the peak of Misaka after Ōmononushi and Ashiharashio had finished pacifying the land." It is also said that the 17th Emperor, {{ill|Emperor Richū|Q329704|qid=Q329704}}, visited the shrine. On that occasion, Emperor Richū reportedly said, "The flow of this river is exceedingly beautiful," and from this the entire region came to be called "Minō District." Furthermore, because a {{ill|Corbiculidae|ar|صخلوديات|arz|صخلوديات|ca|Corbicúlids|cdo|Liù-giāng|ceb|Corbiculidae|de|Körbchenmuscheln (Familie)|es|Corbiculidae|fa|صدف‌های دوکفه‌ای سبدی|fr|Corbiculidae|hak|Hán-é|ja|シジミ|ky|Корбикулдар|nl|Corbiculidae|nv|Łeeyiʼ chʼosh bitsʼaʼí tsʼaaʼígíí|pl|Korbikulowate|ro|Corbiculidae|sv|Corbiculidae|tr|Corbiculidae|vi|Họ Hến|war|Corbiculidae|zh|花蜆科|zh_min_nan|Lâ-á|zh_yue|蜆|qid=Q1796597}} crawled up onto the Emperor's dining table, the area came to be known as Shijimi (志染)<ref name="yuisyo">[https://misaka-jinja.com/yuisyo/ Misaka Shrine official website - History of Misaka Shrine] </ref>.

it was designated as a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=shrine receiving offerings of sacred food and cloth}}<ref name="yuisyo"></ref>.

Within Miki City, there are a total of eight shrines called "'''Misaka'''," including this Misaka Shrine, as well as '''Misaka Shrine''' (三坂神社), '''Misaka Shrine''' (美坂神社), '''Misaka Shrine''' (御酒神社), and others.

=== Precincts ===
The main hall and the worship hall, which is structurally connected to it, face a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Noh stage}} and a shrine office in front. The area behind the main hall is a grove where {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=yin-yang stones}} are enshrined<ref name="photo">[https://misaka-jinja.com/gallery/ Misaka Shrine official website - Photo]</ref>.

Previously held on the first Day of the Boar after {{ill|Lunar New Year|Q1944136|qid=Q1944136}}, it was changed to February 11, {{ill|National Foundation Day|Q12981823|qid=Q12981823}}, from {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shōwa 55}}. Six archers each shoot 2 {{ill|Arrow|Q45922|qid=Q45922}}s per round over 5 rounds, for a total of 10 arrows aimed at a {{ill|target|Q11269217|qid=Q11269217}} approximately 20 meters away. If an arrow hits the center of the target, it foretells a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=bountiful harvest}} for that year. If it hits the area marked "oni" (demon) sealed on the back of the target, it is called "[[Wikt:破邪|haja]] kenshō" (breaking evil and revealing righteousness), meaning that evil is defeated and correct principles are made manifest in the world. Originally, the archers would perform {{ill|Misogi|Q1936265|qid=Q1936265}} in the {{ill|Shijimi River|Q11491046|qid=Q11491046}} beside the shrine, then silently receive {{ill|Omiki|Q3313722|qid=Q3313722}} in the "Nagatoko no Gi" ceremony at the {{ill|Haiden (Shinto)|Q3125745|qid=Q3125745}}, but this is now omitted. In addition, the "Urayasu no Mai" dance is performed by a {{ill|Miko|Q1047139|qid=Q1047139}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Sarutahiko}} performs the "Tenchi-barai, Shihō-barai" (purification of heaven and earth, purification of the four directions), and finally {{ill|mochimaki|Q11666809|qid=Q11666809}} (mochi-throwing) is held.
